Thanks for the demo earlier this week. Two commercial/ops items came up in our procurement sync that I wanted to run by you before we move to SOW:

2) Support/on-call — we need clarity on what counts as "on-call" hours and whether we can cap after-hours response for non-critical issues (we’re fine with P1s 24/7).

Mike — thanks for the quick note and great to hear the sync went well. High level answers below and I’ve attached a short commercial offer (ApexMed-Commercial-Offer-v3.pdf) and draft SOW for visibility.

Option A (standard): 100% platform fee due on subscription start; support as per published Premium 24/7 for P1, business hours for P2/P3. No amortization.

Option B (defer): Up to 50% of the platform fee can be deferred and issued as implementation credits that offset monthly consumption for the first 6 months. Credits do not reduce the public list price for committed consumption and are not refundable; they apply only to usage/consumption invoices. Requires a 12-month minimum commitment.

Option C (accelerated): Defer 75% of the platform fee if ApexMed takes a 24-month committed consumption tier and buys the oncall retainer (discounted).

On support/on-call: we can tighten the definition so non-P1 (severity 2/3) after-hours is handled during business hours the next day unless you purchase an on-call retainer that guarantees after-hours triage within 4 hours for P2.

Practical impact: deferring moves revenue recognition for that portion into implementation credits (accounting teams treat as contra revenue/credit). Finance has to sign off, but we do this frequently for strategic pilots.

Next steps: Vanessa — can you confirm how much flexibility we have on the defer percentage and whether we need FOA from finance? Hannah — I’ve attached the SOW draft for redlines.

Mike — if any of those options are acceptable I’ll put the selected option into the commercial PDF and send a DocuSign for the commercial terms + SOW.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ApexMed-Commercial-Offer-v3.pdf, SOW-draft-ApexMed.docx

Alex / Hannah — quick internal note on what finance will accept and recommended counter: 

- Finance will allow up to 50% deferred as implementation credits for deals with >$250k TCV and a 12-month minimum. Anything more requires CFO approval.
- If we defer, we should require a clause that credits expire after 6 months and cannot be transferred.
- For on-call: offer a capped retainer (40 hrs/mo) that guarantees 4hr P2 triage; standard P1 24/7 remains. Pricing: retainer at $12k/mo, or $9k/mo if they take 24-mo commit.

My suggested commercial counter (single line): Defer 50% platform fee as implementation credits applied against consumption over first 6 months; on-call retainer optional at $12k/mo (or $9k/mo with 24-mo commit). If procurement agrees, we finalize SOW and route to DocuSign.

Hannah — please confirm SOW redline around credit expiry and include a short clause limiting credits to usage only.

Vanessa
